## TL;DR
Human-assigned tasks now get a `## Step-by-step guide` requirement: PM and engineer prompts demand it, `repoos new`/`update`/the API warn when it is missing, the scaffold includes the heading, and `repoos update --section` edits it alone. This round fixes review pass 5: section scanning was fence-unaware.

## Work and rationale
- `src/core/task.ts`: `nextSection` and `collectActivityEntries` now track fenced code with the shared `isMarkdownFenceClose`, so a `## ` line inside a fence no longer ends a section. That fixes `extractSection`, `replaceSection`, `removeSection` (so `repoos update --section "Step-by-step guide"` no longer corrupts a guide containing a fenced example) and acceptance-criteria parsing in `human-step-tags.ts`.
- New table tests in `src/core/task-section-fence.test.ts` for extract, replace and remove with a fenced `## ` line, and a closing-fence-with-info-string case.
- Earlier rounds (already on the branch): warning logic, scaffold, prompts, docs, drawer banner; merged main and kept other tasks' bookkeeping off the branch; restored the reviewed commit into history so the round-relative diff base resolves.

## Approaches tried
Fixing only `replaceSection` was rejected: the same unaware scan feeds three section helpers and the activity collector, so the shared scanner was fixed once.

## Challenges and blockers
Five unrelated `src/core` tests (attachment-migration, canary, git-maintenance-lsof, task-dependencies) fail when run under bare vitest in this worktree; they are environment-sensitive and untouched by this diff.

## Key learnings
Any hand-rolled markdown heading scan must track fences; one shared helper per concern avoids the review loop of finding each copy separately.
